title: Stoker metadata — media
description: `games/<id>/media.json`: the game's artwork and media reel. A file apart from `game.json` because the images are inlined and make it large: editing a description should not mean a diff next to megabytes of base64. Images are in the document; trailers are not — they are tens of megabytes each, and are recorded by their source and their hash.

artwork.description: The four slots a library draws a game or a DLC with, by the names Steam's library cache uses.

capsule.description: Portrait box art, 2:3 (600×900 on Steam) — what a library grid shows.

header.description: The wide store header (460×215 on Steam).

hero.description: The wide banner behind a game's page.

logo.description: The transparent wordmark laid over the hero.

reel.description: Screenshots and trailers, in the order the store page shows them — for Steam every trailer in its order, then every screenshot in its order.

trailer.description: A trailer. Its bytes are not in the repository: an instance fetches them from the source and checks them against the hashes here.

highlight.description: The store marks it as one to lead with. Recorded, not used to reorder: the store page keeps its order whatever is marked.

sourceKey.description: The store's own id for the trailer, so a re-import recognises it.

track.description: One stored track of a trailer, as Stoker keeps it: fragmented MP4.
